lines.en: Rina, how was your first night on stage? You looked pale before the curtain went up. I was worried you might faint.
lines.pt: Rina, como foi a sua primeira noite no palco? Você estava pálida antes de abrir a cortina. Fiquei com medo de que você desmaiasse.

lines.en: Honestly, I had never felt so nervous in my life. My hands were shaking, and my mouth was completely dry.
lines.pt: Sinceramente, nunca me senti tão nervosa na vida. Minhas mãos tremiam, e a minha boca estava completamente seca.

lines.en: But you had rehearsed for months! I had never seen anyone prepare so carefully. You even practiced your lines in the car.
lines.pt: Mas você ensaiou por meses! Eu nunca tinha visto ninguém se preparar com tanto cuidado. Você até ensaiava as falas no carro.

lines.en: I know, and that’s what made it worse. The audience was enormous, bigger than anything I’d ever seen. I could hardly breathe.
lines.pt: Eu sei, e foi isso que piorou. A plateia era enorme, maior do que qualquer uma que eu já tinha visto. Mal conseguia respirar.

lines.en: Well, you hid it perfectly. When you walked on, nobody could have guessed. What was going through your mind?
lines.pt: Bem, você disfarçou perfeitamente. Quando entrou, ninguém poderia imaginar. O que passava pela sua cabeça?

lines.en: Mostly, I kept repeating my first line. Then somebody coughed, and there was such a long silence that I blushed under the lights.
lines.pt: Basicamente, eu repetia a minha primeira fala. Então alguém tossiu, e houve um silêncio tão longo que fiquei vermelha sob as luzes.

lines.en: That was the moment I held my breath! But then you smiled, and the whole room relaxed. It felt like magic.
lines.pt: Foi o momento em que prendi a respiração! Mas aí você sorriu, e a sala toda relaxou. Pareceu mágica.

lines.en: Thanks, but I didn’t feel like a star until the final scene. After the last line, the applause started, and I almost cried.
lines.pt: Obrigada, mas só me senti uma estrela na cena final. Depois da última fala, os aplausos começaram, e quase chorei.

lines.en: You were so relieved that you hugged the whole cast backstage! Even the director got a hug, and he hates being touched.
lines.pt: Você ficou tão aliviada que abraçou o elenco todo nos bastidores! Até o diretor ganhou um abraço, e ele odeia que o toquem.

lines.en: I know! I had never been so happy and so tired at the same time. I slept for eleven hours afterward.
lines.pt: Eu sei! Nunca tinha ficado tão feliz e tão cansada ao mesmo tempo. Dormi onze horas depois.

lines.en: Well, you deserve it. Tomorrow’s show will feel easier, I promise, and I’ll be in the front row, cheering as loudly as I can.
lines.pt: Bem, você merece. O show de amanhã vai parecer mais fácil, prometo, e vou estar na primeira fila, torcendo o mais alto que puder.

facts.label: Sentimentos extremos
facts.sub: Algo nunca vivido antes do momento passado: I had never felt so nervous. Com substantivo: such a big audience. Consequência: so… that.

facts.label: Nunca tinha
facts.sub: Use had never + particípio para dizer que algo era uma experiência nova num momento do passado: I had never felt so nervous. Never fica entre had e o particípio, sem inversão.

facts.label: Tão
facts.sub: Use so antes de adjetivo ou advérbio (so nervous, so carefully) e such antes de substantivo (such a big audience). Ambos intensificam o sentimento. Não misture: nunca diga such nervous.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Had never felt so nervous gives emphasis.
We say “I never had felt so nervous”.
items.why: We say I had never felt.

items.s: So goes before an adjective, such before a noun.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.

extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Had never felt so nervous gives emphasis. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “I never had felt so nervous”. → Falso (We say I had never felt.)
So goes before an adjective, such before a noun. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: The night of the curtain · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Saturday night in a small theatre in Auckland. The lights go down. Zoe stands behind the curtain with a paper in her hand. It is her first show in front of real people. The next day, her friend Abby meets her at a café. Abby wants to know how it felt.

“Zoe, how was your first night on stage? You looked pale before the curtain went up.” says Abby. “Honestly, I had never felt so nervous in my life. My hands were shaking, and my mouth was completely dry.” says Zoe. “But you had rehearsed for months. I had never seen anyone prepare so carefully.” says Abby.

paragraphs: “He said I had handled the pressure better than anyone he had worked with, which made me blush.” says Zoe. “You earned it. Tomorrow you will not be so nervous, and the applause will be even louder.” says Abby. Zoe smiles and shows her a message from the director. He offers her a bigger role.
